line: Secondary manifold's due for a flush. You could do it. But I've got autos on standby. They're reliable. They don't flirt.
Secondary manifold's due for a flush. I'd say you're just the one to do it... but the automatics handle it every cycle.
That latch rattles when we hit 0.7c. You'd think it was a problem. It's not. I have a clamp for that. I'll use it next time I'm bored.
Sensor's drifted. You could recalibrate it. No, the auto-align kicks in every ten hours.
Grease on the landing gear is overdue. You could do it, but the bots handle it. Just making sure you're not bored.
My forward sensor's off by a hair. You could recalibrate it if you wanted. The automatics do it better, but they're slow.
Forward viewport's got a film on it. You could clean it if you wanted. It's just a polymer buildup — the scrubbers handle it.
My secondary manifold's due for flushing. You'd be good at it. Too much flow for the automateds — they're not built for finesse.
My viewport's fogged up. You could wipe it. If you had the right solvent.
Air filter's due. You could swap it now... or wait. The auto's been running fine since the last cycle.
There's a panel latch that rattles when we hit 45 knots. Someone's going to have to check it. Oh, wait — I've got a dampener for that. It's just rattling.
There's a cable run behind the galley bulkhead that's coiled like a bad habit. I could let you untangle it... but the automatics are patient.
My collar's got a scuff. You could polish it if you wanted. The sensors don't care, though — they're all on the inside.
My intakes are clean, but the filters need swapping. You could do it. If you had the right tools.
Filter's loose in port three. You could swap it. Automatics hold it for now.
